text: Article 49 of the 1995 Constitution of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right, having notified respective governmental bodies in advance, to assemble with other people peacefully and without arms, to organise meetings, demonstrations, protests and marches, and to stage pickets.

Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, advance written notification is required in order to agree upon the place and time of an assembly and upon the route of a march, with the purpose of enabling the relevant local executive authority to take necessary measures.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, the notification must be done in writing five days before the demonstration.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: Article 8 §§ IV and V of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to issue relevant orders so as to prohibit a public assembly.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: Article 8 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to issue relevant orders so as to stop a public assembly.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: Article 9 §§ II and VII of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to restrict or change the place, route and/or time of a public assembly.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: Article 9 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provides the relevant local executive authority with broad powers to designate specific areas for public assemblies.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § I(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power, when necessary, to stop an assembly which has not been notified to the authorities beforehand, save for spontaneous assemblies.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § I(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend and remove from the place where an event is being held persons who came carrying weapons, rocks, pieces of wood and glass, clubs that may pose a threat to people's life and safety or damage property, as well as explosives, flammables, or radioactive materials.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § II(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to order the organisers and participants of an assembly to use all available opportunities to stop the assembly and to disperse, with regard to the execution of orders specified under Article 8 §§ V and VI of that Law.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § II(3) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to warn organisers and participants that physical force or exceptional measures will be used against them if the order to stop the assembly and to disperse is not complied with.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § II(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to use physical force or exceptional measures in order to stop an assembly and disperse participants, in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § II(5) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend persons not complying with the order to stop an assembly and disperse.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 14 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the use of physical force or exceptional measures by police officers in all circumstances must be proportionate to an existing threat.
section_path: B. Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998

text: At the material time, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen manats (AZN).
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with the lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 376.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that if it is impossible for the lawyer chosen by the person against whom administrative-offence proceedings are being carried out to attend, a judge shall appoint a lawyer for that person, in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 376.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that if a person subjected to an administrative arrest has no possibility to hire a lawyer due to his or her financial situation, his or her legal assistance shall be funded by the State, and in this case a lawyer may not refuse to carry out his or her duties.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 396.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that an authorised official may use measures to secure administrative-offence proceedings, including administrative arrest (Article 396.1.2), in order to prevent administrative offences, to establish the identity of a person, to draw up an administrative-offence report if this cannot be done at the place of the administrative offence and if the drawing up of a report is important, to ensure the correct and timely examination of administrative-offence cases, and to ensure the implementation of decisions in administrative-offence cases.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 398.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that administrative arrest, that is the short-term restriction of an individual's liberty, may be applied in exceptional circumstances when deemed necessary for ensuring the correct and timely examination of an administrative-offence case or for the implementation of a decision in an administrative-offence case, except for instances set out in legislation.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that a copy of the administrative-offence report shall be given to an individual who is subject to the administrative-offence proceedings or to a representative of a legal entity.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 414.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that a report concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be sent to a judge for examination immediately after it has been drawn up.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 provided that cases concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be examined on the day of receipt by the court of an administrative-offence report, and cases against persons subjected to administrative arrest shall be examined at the latest within 48 hours of their arrest.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: Under Article 368 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000, a public prosecutor has a right to participate in administrative proceedings.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 enumerates the participants of administrative proceedings and their rights and obligations.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: Chapter 28 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) of 2000 does not mention the prosecution — a police officer, public prosecutor or any other public official representing the prosecution — as a participant of the proceedings.
section_path: C. Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 ("the CAO")

text: The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, in document CommDH(2011)33 dated 29 September 2011, noted that his attention was drawn to the wave of arrests of activists and political opponents in connection with protests held in Baku in March and April 2011.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: According to information received by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, the protests held in Baku in March and April 2011 were sometimes dispersed with excessive force, and the work of journalists was hindered.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe noted that the organisers of protests in Baku in March and April 2011 were denied permission to demonstrate in a central square and other places in the city centre in Baku, and were instead authorised to hold a demonstration in the outskirts of the city.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe noted that several persons were detained on grounds of violating public order in connection with protests held in Baku in March and April 2011.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe noted that six opposition activists were sentenced on 25 August 2011 for participating in actions causing disturbance of public order, following trials whose conformity with human rights standards has been called into question.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, in document CommDH(2011)33 dated 29 September 2011, criticised the method of curbing the impact of a demonstration by allowing it to take place only at another time and at a less central location, thereby diminishing significantly the visibility of the rally and its message to the general public.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, in document CommDH(2011)33 dated 29 September 2011, urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that the right to freedom of peaceful assembly is fully guaranteed in Azerbaijan, in accordance with the Court's case-law.
section_path: A. "Observations on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan: Freedom of expression, freedom of association, freedom of peaceful assembly", by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, CommDH(2011)33, 29 September 2011

text: In the Report CommDH(2013)14 dated 6 August 2013, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe Nils Muižnieks noted that the issue of limitations imposed on freedom of assembly had regularly been raised by local and international observers in recent years.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that the most frequent problems encountered in Azerbaijan include the banning of demonstrations in central and easily accessible locations and the use of force to disperse demonstrations which still go ahead, leading to arrests and, in some cases, harsh sentences.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 called on the Azerbaijani authorities to adopt effective measures to prevent the use of force against peaceful protestors by law enforcement officials.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 reiterated the recommendation of the 2010 Report, inviting the Azerbaijani authorities to reform the existing system of internal disciplinary investigations of police ill-treatment and to introduce an independent police complaints body.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that Azerbaijan amended its Law on Freedom of Assembly in 2008, following two opinions adopted by the Council of Europe Venice Commission.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that while the Law on Freedom of Assembly is in line with international standards, undue restrictions of the right to freedom of peaceful assembly are widely reported in practice.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that the problems with freedom of assembly in Azerbaijan mainly stem from the interpretation of Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, which provides for a notification procedure before convening an assembly.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that in 2006, the Venice Commission welcomed the confirmation by representatives of the Government that the requirement in the Law on Freedom of Assembly was for notification and not for a prior permission to hold the assembly.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that in 2006, the Venice Commission noted that other provisions of the Law on Freedom of Assembly could, as they currently stood, encourage the competent authorities to issue a blanket prohibition as soon as the notification process proves incomplete.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that in 2007, the Venice Commission added that a system of notification is in itself admissible so long as it is only meant to help the authorities cope more easily with the practical problems involved with the holding of an assembly.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that in 2007, the Venice Commission stressed that it is important that assemblies can be held with a presumption of legality so as to avoid any chilling effect on organisers and participants.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that the Azerbaijani authorities confirmed that the legislation does not require permission for rallies, but the authorities appear to have interpreted it as requiring such permission, and a system of authorisation has in practice replaced the system of notification.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that peaceful protesters have been effectively banned from demonstrating in central Baku since 2006, despite advanced notification of the assemblies.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that several requests by the political opposition or civil society to hold demonstrations were allegedly denied or, when allowed, organisers were obliged to have them in areas very remote from the city centre of Baku.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 expressed concern about the way the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 is currently being implemented in Azerbaijan and called on the authorities to assess the functioning of that law.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 called on the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no authorisation is required for the holding of public demonstrations and that the system of notification is applied in accordance with European standards.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 welcomed the announced publication by the Azerbaijani authorities of a list of locations where demonstrations will be made possible, and called for these to include adequate locations in the centre of Baku and other cities.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the authorities should seek to facilitate and protect public assemblies at the organisers' preferred location, given the need for tolerance in a democratic society.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted a concern relating to the reported non-implementation of due process standards in proceedings brought against participants in unauthorised demonstrations in Azerbaijan.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Report CommDH(2013)14 called on the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure the full respect of fair trial guarantees for protesters.
section_path: B. Report by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013, CommDH(2013)14, 6 August 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that the Baku municipal authorities have implemented a blanket ban on all opposition demonstrations in the city center since early 2006.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that the authorities have broken up unsanctioned demonstrations — often with violence — and have arrested and imprisoned peaceful protestors, organizers, and participants.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that the misdemeanor trials of those charged for involvement in unsanctioned protests are perfunctory.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that while the constitution of Azerbaijan stipulates that groups may peacefully assemble after simply notifying the relevant government body in advance, in practice authorities require that gatherings obtain a permit issued by local municipalities.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that municipal authorities have effectively banned all forms of peaceful protest from the center of Baku and instead force all demonstrations into designated zones on the outskirts of the city.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) stated that such a blanket ban on freedom of assembly in the central areas of Baku violates Azerbaijan's international obligations to respect freedom of assembly and expression.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that for several years police have dispersed, at times violently, peaceful protests in Baku's center.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that in the days before and during the Eurovision Song Contest held in Baku in May 2012, police broke up several protests in the city's center and briefly detained dozens of peaceful demonstrators.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that in 2011, when activists inspired by the uprisings in the Middle East and North Africa launched protests in Azerbaijan, the government responded by arresting hundreds of protesters, activists, and journalists.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that several protesters in Azerbaijan in 2011 were convicted of public order offences and imprisoned for up to three years.
section_path: C. Report by Human Rights Watch, "Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent", 2013

text: The Human Rights Watch Report 'Tightening the Screws: Azerbaijan's Crackdown on Civil Society and Dissent' (2013) noted that the Azerbaijani authorities regularly use administrative or misdemeanor charges to lock up people for organizing or participating in unsanctioned rallies, then prosecuting and convicting them in perfunctory trials.
